
  name: MERN CI/CD Pipeline

  # Run when code is pushed to main, or manually.
  on:
    push:
      branches:
        - main
    workflow_dispatch:

  # Permissions needed for this workflow.
  permissions:
    contents: read

  jobs:
    build-and-deploy:
      # GitHub provides a temporary Ubuntu machine.
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      steps:
        # Step 1: Download our repository code.
        - name: Checkout code
          uses: actions/checkout@v4    
          # downloads the repository's code into the runner

        # Step 2: Build the frontend to catch build errors.
        - name: Build frontend
          run: |
            cd frontend
            npm ci
            npm run build
        # If the build fails, the workflow stops at this step. This catches many frontend errors before deployment. add TESTS later

        # Step 3: Build the backend Docker image.
        - name: Build backend image
          run: |
            docker build \
              -t ayushg001/test-devops-backend:${{ github.sha }} \
              ./backend
              
  # ${{ github.sha }} is a GitHub Actions expression that supplies the commit's full SHA, a unique identifier for that revision of your code.


        # Step 4: Build the frontend Docker image.
        - name: Build frontend image
          run: |
            docker build \
              -t ayushg001/test-devops-frontend:${{ github.sha }} \
              ./frontend

  # If you deploy latest every time, it's harder to identify which exact version is running. A commit SHA gives every build its own tag, making rollbacks and debugging easier.

        # Step 5: Log in to Docker Hub.
        - name: Login to Docker Hub
          uses: docker/login-action@v3
          with:
            username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
            password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

        # Step 6: Upload both images to Docker Hub.
        - name: Push Docker images
          run: |
            docker push ayushg001/test-devops-backend:${{ github.sha }}
            docker push ayushg001/test-devops-frontend:${{ github.sha }}

        # Step 7: Connect to the Linux server and deploy.
        - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
          uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
          env:
            IMAGE_TAG: ${{ github.sha }}
          with:
            host: ${{ secrets.SSH_HOST }}
            username: ${{ secrets.SSH_USERNAME }}
            key: ${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
            envs: IMAGE_TAG
            script: |
              set -e

              kubectl set image deployment/backend \
                backend=ayushg001/test-devops-backend:$IMAGE_TAG \
                -n test-devops

              kubectl set image deployment/frontend \
                frontend=ayushg001/test-devops-frontend:$IMAGE_TAG \
                -n test-devops           

              kubectl rollout status deployment/backend \
                -n test-devops --timeout=180s

              kubectl rollout status deployment/frontend \
                -n test-devops --timeout=180s

  #  - set -e              stops the script when a command fails.
  # - set image            changes the image used by a container in an existing workload.
  # - deployment/backend   identifies the Deployment named backend.
  # - backend=...          identifies the container named backend and the new image it should use.
  # - -n test-devops       selects your existing Kubernetes namespace.

  # Kubernetes then creates replacement Pods using the new image and gradually replaces the old Pods, according to the Deployment's rollout strategy.  

  # ->
  # wait for each Deployment to finish rolling out, with a maximum wait of 180 seconds per command. If a rollout doesn't complete successfully, the workflow reports a failure rather than silently treating the deployment as successful.



  # Continuous Integration (CI)
  # The workflow checks out the code, builds the frontend, and builds both Docker images. Build errors stop the pipeline before the images are published.

  # Continuous Delivery / Deployment (CD)
  # The workflow pushes the images to Docker Hub, connects to your Linux server, updates Kubernetes, and waits for the rollouts to complete.
